title: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH)
summary: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia affects the adrenal glands, which make important hormones. The most common type, 21-hydroxylase deficiency, means the body makes too little of some hormones and too much of others.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the CYP21A2 gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has CAH. It ranges from a serious form noticed soon after birth to milder forms found later. It is managed for life with hormone treatment from a specialist team.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has CAH. Could I be a carrier?
What does a test for the CYP21A2 gene involve?
card_summary: The adrenal glands don't make the right balance of hormones. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Managed for life with hormone treatment from a specialist team.
care: Specialist endocrinology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
counsellor_questions: Which carrier test is right for me?
If I'm a carrier, could my partner be tested too?
What treatment and support exist today?
